text: Advanced economies should legally redefine the standard full-time workweek to four days with no reduction in base pay for most full-time employees.
Countries should reintroduce wolves, lynx, and other apex predators to restore degraded ecosystems even when rural communities and livestock farmers object.
Mass university expansion raised credential inflation more than it expanded genuine opportunity.
Major cities should ban private cars from central districts entirely rather than rely on congestion pricing alone.
Teaching formal logic, probability, and statistical reasoning from primary school onward would do more for democratic resilience than any media-literacy curriculum.
Governments should heavily tax the production of fast fashion to subsidize more local and sustainable textile manufacturing even if clothing prices rise for lower-income consumers.
Embryo screening for non-disease traits such as height, appearance, or predicted cognition should be legally restricted even if the underlying technology becomes more reliable.
Four-day school weeks harm student learning more than they help school districts save money and retain staff.
Universal pre-K programs produce lasting educational and social gains large enough to justify their public cost.
Governments should ban social-media accounts for children under sixteen rather than rely mainly on parental controls and softer design changes.
Social media use is a primary driver of the teen mental-health crisis rather than merely a visible correlate of deeper problems.
Restricting short-term rentals in high-demand city neighborhoods reduces rents and displacement more than it harms local incomes and visitor spending.
Copyright law should create a compulsory licensing scheme for training foundation models on copyrighted text and images, with payment to rightsholders.
Governments should fund and permit de-extinction projects such as woolly mammoth and thylacine revival even when that diverts money and attention from protecting species that are endangered today.
Water-scarce regions should invest primarily in large-scale desalination capacity rather than rely mainly on conservation and rationing.
